front: Il pleuvait quand je suis sorti.
pronunciation: [eel pluh-veh kahn zhuh swee sor-TEE]
back: It was raining when I went out.
context: Background (imparfait) + event (passé composé). The core contrast of French narration.

front: Nous dînions quand il a appelé.
pronunciation: [noo dee-nyohn kahn tee lah ah-puh-LAY]
back: We were having dinner when he called.
context: Ongoing action interrupted by a single event.

front: J'ai vécu trois ans à Lyon.
pronunciation: [zhay vay-kü trwah zahn ah lee-OHN]
back: I lived in Lyon for three years.
context: A closed, finished period with a defined length → passé composé, even if it lasted.

front: Quand je vivais à Lyon, je prenais le tram tous les jours.
pronunciation: [kahn zhuh vee-veh ah lee-OHN, zhuh pruh-neh luh TRAM too lay ZHOOR]
back: When I lived in Lyon, I took the tram every day.
context: Habits in that period → imparfait.

front: Hier, j'ai pris le bus à huit heures.
pronunciation: [YEHR, zhay pree luh büs ah wee TUHR]
back: Yesterday I took the bus at eight.
context: A single, dated action → passé composé.

front: Ce matin, il faisait froid, donc j'ai mis mon manteau.
pronunciation: [suh mah-TAN, eel fuh-zeh FRWAH, dohnk zhay mee mohn mahn-TOH]
back: This morning it was cold, so I put on my coat.
context: Situation (imparfait) leading to a reaction (passé composé).

front: Elle était en train de cuisiner quand la lumière s'est éteinte.
pronunciation: [el ay-teh tahn tran duh kwee-zee-NAY kahn lah lü-myehr seh tay-TANT]
back: She was cooking when the lights went out.
context: 'Être en train de' in the imparfait stresses the action in progress.

front: Soudain, la porte s'est ouverte.
pronunciation: [soo-DAN, lah port seh too-VEHRT]
back: Suddenly, the door opened.
context: 'Soudain', 'tout à coup', 'à ce moment-là' introduce events → passé composé.

front: Tout à coup, j'ai entendu un bruit.
pronunciation: [too tah KOO, zhay ahn-tahn-dü an BRWEE]
back: All of a sudden, I heard a noise.
context: 'Tout à coup' = all of a sudden.

front: D'habitude, je me levais tôt, mais ce jour-là, je me suis réveillé à midi.
pronunciation: [dah-bee-TÜD, zhuh muh luh-veh TOH, meh suh zhoor-LAH, zhuh muh swee ray-veh-yay ah mee-DEE]
back: Usually I got up early, but that day I woke up at noon.
context: Habit (imparfait) vs exception on a specific day (passé composé).

front: Il était midi, le soleil brillait et les enfants jouaient.
pronunciation: [ee lay-teh mee-DEE, luh soh-lay bree-YEH ay lay zahn-fahn zhoo-EH]
back: It was noon, the sun was shining and the children were playing.
context: A whole scene of description: all imparfait.

front: Je suis arrivé, j'ai posé mon sac et je me suis assis.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zah-ree-VAY, zhay poh-zay mohn SAK ay zhuh muh swee zah-SEE]
back: I arrived, put down my bag and sat down.
context: A sequence of completed actions: all passé composé.

front: Quand j'ai vu le prix, j'ai compris pourquoi il n'y avait personne.
pronunciation: [kahn zhay vü luh PREE, zhay kohm-pree poor-kwah eel nyah-veh pehr-SUN]
back: When I saw the price, I understood why there was nobody there.
context: Events (vu, compris) + a state (il n'y avait personne).

front: Je ne savais pas qu'il était marié.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh sah-veh pah keel ay-teh mah-RYAY]
back: I didn't know he was married.
context: States of knowledge and being → imparfait.

front: J'ai su la nouvelle hier soir.
pronunciation: [zhay sü lah noo-vel yehr SWAHR]
back: I found out the news last night.
context: 'Savoir' in the passé composé = to find out (a moment), not to know (a state).

front: Je connaissais déjà la ville.
pronunciation: [zhuh koh-neh-seh day-zhah lah VEEL]
back: I already knew the city.
context: 'Connaître' in the imparfait = to know (state).

front: J'ai connu ma femme à l'université.
pronunciation: [zhay koh-nü mah fam ah lü-nee-vehr-see-TAY]
back: I met my wife at university.
context: 'Connaître' in the passé composé = to meet (for the first time).

front: Il voulait partir, mais il est resté.
pronunciation: [eel voo-leh par-TEER, meh ee leh res-TAY]
back: He wanted to leave, but he stayed.
context: A wish (imparfait) vs what actually happened (passé composé).

front: J'ai voulu l'appeler, mais je n'ai pas pu.
pronunciation: [zhay voo-lü lah-puh-LAY, meh zhuh neh pah PÜ]
back: I tried to call him, but I couldn't.
context: 'Vouloir' in the passé composé = to try/decide at a given moment.

front: Il faisait nuit quand nous sommes arrivés à l'hôtel.
pronunciation: [eel fuh-zeh NWEE kahn noo sum zah-ree-vay ah loh-TEL]
back: It was dark when we got to the hotel.
context: Setting + arrival.

front: Pendant mon enfance, je passais mes étés chez mes grands-parents.
pronunciation: [pahn-dahn mohn nahn-FAHNS, zhuh pah-seh may zay-tay shay may grahn-pah-RAHN]
back: During my childhood, I spent my summers at my grandparents'.
context: Repeated habit over a period → imparfait.

front: Pendant les vacances, nous avons visité dix villes.
pronunciation: [pahn-dahn lay vah-KAHNS, noo zah-vohn vee-zee-tay dee VEEL]
back: During the holidays, we visited ten cities.
context: Countable, completed actions → passé composé, even with 'pendant'.

front: Elle avait l'air fatiguée, alors je lui ai proposé un café.
pronunciation: [el ah-veh lehr fah-tee-GAY, ah-lor zhuh lwee ay proh-poh-zay an kah-FAY]
back: She looked tired, so I offered her a coffee.
context: Appearance (imparfait) → action (passé composé).

front: Comme il n'y avait plus de pain, je suis allé à la boulangerie.
pronunciation: [kum eel nyah-veh plü duh PAN, zhuh swee zah-lay ah lah boo-lahn-zhuh-REE]
back: As there was no bread left, I went to the bakery.
context: 'Comme' (as/since) introduces the cause, usually imparfait.

front: On regardait un film quand l'orage a éclaté.
pronunciation: [ohn ruh-gar-deh tan FEELM kahn loh-rahzh ah ay-klah-TAY]
back: We were watching a film when the storm broke.
context: 'Éclater' = to break out (storm, war).

front: L'année dernière, j'ai couru un marathon.
pronunciation: [lah-nay dehr-NYEHR, zhay koo-rü an mah-rah-TOHN]
back: Last year I ran a marathon.
context: Single achievement → passé composé.

front: Quand j'étais étudiant, je courais tous les matins.
pronunciation: [kahn zhay-teh zay-tü-DYAHN, zhuh koo-reh too lay mah-TAN]
back: When I was a student, I ran every morning.
context: Repeated habit → imparfait.

front: Il y avait du monde, donc nous avons attendu.
pronunciation: [eel yah-veh dü MOHND, dohnk noo zah-vohn ah-tahn-DÜ]
back: There were a lot of people, so we waited.
context: State → consequence.

front: Elle a toujours aimé la musique.
pronunciation: [el ah too-zhoor eh-MAY lah mü-ZEEK]
back: She has always loved music.
context: 'A toujours aimé' = has always loved (up to now).

front: J'étais sur le point de partir quand tu es arrivé.
pronunciation: [zhay-teh sür luh pwan duh par-TEER kahn tü eh tah-ree-VAY]
back: I was about to leave when you arrived.
context: 'Être sur le point de' = to be about to.

front: Il a plu toute la journée.
pronunciation: [ee lah PLÜ toot lah zhoor-NAY]
back: It rained all day.
context: A closed period seen as a whole → passé composé.

front: Ma grand-mère faisait le meilleur gâteau du monde.
pronunciation: [mah grahn-mehr fuh-zeh luh meh-yuhr gah-TOH dü MOHND]
back: My grandmother used to make the best cake in the world.
context: Nostalgic habit → imparfait.

front: Le jour où j'ai eu mon diplôme, j'étais tellement fier !
pronunciation: [luh zhoor oo zhay ü mohn dee-PLOHM, zhay-teh tel-mahn FYEHR]
back: The day I got my degree, I was so proud!
context: Event (j'ai eu) + feeling at that time (j'étais).

front: Il était une fois un roi qui avait trois filles. Un jour, il est tombé malade.
pronunciation: [ee lay-teh tün FWAH an RWAH kee ah-veh trwah FEE. an ZHOOR, ee leh tohm-bay mah-LAD]
back: Once upon a time there was a king who had three daughters. One day, he fell ill.
context: Classic story structure: setting in the imparfait, then 'un jour' + passé composé.

front: Bref, c'était une soirée inoubliable.
pronunciation: [BREF, seh-teh tün swah-ray ee-noo-blee-YAH-bluh]
back: In short, it was an unforgettable evening.
context: Closing judgments are often in the imparfait: 'c'était génial'.
